stories.headline: Missing Deadline Behind Punjab's Chief Justice Dispute
stories.title: Missing Deadline Behind Punjab's Chief Justice Dispute
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: The appointment of Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, notified on 5 September 2026, has drawn an unusually public objection from the State of Punjab, whose Cabinet resolved the next day that the appointment had been made without the State's consent.
The real question, however, is not whether Punjab's consent was required, for it plainly was not.
It is whether a State that has been asked for its views, and has not given them, can be said to have been consulted when the rules prescribe no time within which it must answer.
That question arises because the Memorandum of Procedure treats the two kinds of High Court appointment differently.
Where the Chief Justice of a High Court proposes a new judge, the State Government has six weeks to comment.
If it does not reply, paragraph 14 permits the Union to presume that the Governor, that is, the Chief Minister, “has nothing to add”, and to proceed.
Where the appointment is of the Chief Justice, paragraph 6 prescribes no period at all.

It is submitted that this gap, rather than the conduct of either party, lies at the heart of the dispute, and that it can be closed by a single amendment to a document the Government has been expected to revise since 2015.
The Collegium recommended Justice Mishra on 6 August 2026, and the Law Ministry sought Punjab's views between 10 and 12 August.
Haryana, which shares the High Court, responded, as did the Governors of both States; Punjab's elected government did not.
The Union notified the appointment on 5 September together with seven others, and the Chief Minister stayed away from the oath two days later.

The Additional Solicitor General has since maintained that a week or two was ample time for the State to respond, while Punjab's own Cabinet has acknowledged that no time limit is prescribed for the appointment of a Chief Justice.

stories.headline: Karnataka CM Shivakumar seeks Rs 7,142.64 cr drought relief from Centre
stories.title: Karnataka CM Shivakumar seeks Rs 7,142.64 cr drought relief from Centre
stories.summary: Revised demand follows declaration of 177 taluks as drought-affected, with losses pegged at Rs 46,324.50 crore
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - Karnataka seeks Rs 7,142.64 crore in drought relief from the Centre.
- The state has declared 177 of 240 taluks drought-hit.
- A Central team will assess the drought situation across Karnataka for three days.
Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Saturday urged the Centre to provide Rs 7,142.64 crore in drought relief to the state, citing severe hardship faced by farmers and the general public.
The state had earlier sought Rs 3,705.30 crore under National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) norms.
The revised demand follows the declaration of 177 taluks as drought-affected, with losses estimated at Rs 46,324.50 crore, the chief minister's office said.
"If farmers suffer, everything comes to a standstill.

Therefore, the central government should come to the aid of the state's farmers," Shivakumar said during discussions with a Central Inter-Ministerial team led by Ajit Kumar Sahu, joint secretary in the Union Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
Of Karnataka's 240 taluks, 217 have been identified as drought-affected, while 177 have been officially declared drought-hit, according to the statement.
The government said the taluks were identified through a scientific assessment and in accordance with the Centre's disaster-management guidelines.
Shivakumar said he and Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara had not witnessed such hardship among people in their four decades of public life.
He said a special legislative session was convened to understand problems faced by elected representatives and farmers, with around 150 MLAs raising issues concerning their constituencies.
